## Summary

Execute the reviewed guide, not a one-coder-per-ceremony split. Unit completion is partial evidence; only composed observable behavior plus independent review satisfies the product acceptance criteria.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Keep every unit independently implementable against frozen injected contracts.
- Expose and prove every accepted capability through the actual packaged CLI and source Builder workflow.
- Preserve the complete manual Builder/harness record, archive and owned-resource safety even while shipping awaits authorization.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No source changes to pij, Flowspace or deployed/global skills.
- No silent model/root fallback, new competing flow state, remote push/PR/merge or unowned resource removal.

<a id="testing-strategy"></a>

## Testing Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| approach | Hybrid: test-first for state transitions, readiness predicates, allocation/preservation and failure paths; direct behavioral smoke for the public CLI. |
| rationale | The risk is false success or data loss, not syntax; injected fakes prove ordering/refusals and disposable real Git repositories prove the user-facing lifecycle. |
| focus_areas | Non-vacuity; atomic ordinal reservation; path containment; owner checks; stale evidence; contract drift; pending acknowledgements; composition and review SHA binding; required lifecycle receipts; archive preservation and teardown refusal. |
| excluded | No timing thresholds, mocked internal modules, source-text tests as behavioral proof, or live shared-tree validation by concurrent coders. |
| mock_usage | Existing injected port fakes and real isolated fixtures only; no vi.mock/vi.spyOn/monkey-patching. |

<a id="documentation-strategy"></a>

## Documentation Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| location | Tracked skills/builder and skills/eng-harness-flow source, bundled harness docs/instructions, schema/template examples, and this plan assets directory. |
| rationale | One canonical method and one command surface; examples demonstrate injectable services, good/bad splits, dependency waves, AC ownership and safe closure, while the detailed run log preserves the manual dogfood evidence. |

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

Portable allocation is harness-owned; manual and adopted resources remain external. OMP peers use full local clones, isolated dependencies and actual native-root/message canaries. Typed backpressure is ../../backpressure.dd.json. Source-level design does not substitute for baseline, runtime or product proof.
